target_profile.system_boundary: The selected paxos deployment branch and its in-repository master registration, shared replica runtime, transport, storage hooks, state machine, and client interfaces. Other protocol implementations selected by runReplica are outside this initial inventory.
protocol_contexts: Per-instance Instance records contain cmds, bal, vbal, status, and optional leader bookkeeping.
Replica-wide context includes IsLeader, maxRecvBallot, per-participant defaultBallot, smallestDefaultBallot, and crtInstance.
Leader bookkeeping tracks lastTriedBallot, prepareOKs, acceptOKs, nacks, candidate commands, and pending client proposals.

ReadQuorumSize returns N-F; WriteQuorumSize returns F+1. The deployment caller derives F from configured replica address count, whereas the shared constructor derives N from the master-returned address list.
external_interfaces: Master.Register returns replica identity, node list, readiness, and initial leader indication.
The deployment exports replica methods through Go net/rpc over HTTP.
Protocol message types are registered with a shared numeric RPC table and handler channels.
Client proposals carry ClientId, CommandId, a state.Command, and Timestamp.
The built-in state interface includes command execution against a treemap-backed State.
Optional persistence helpers call Write and Sync on the shared replica's *os.File StableStore.
ownership: runReplica selects the concrete protocol constructor after registration with the master.
Master.Register serializes registration and initial leader selection with master.lock.
paxos.New allocates instance state, registers protocol channels, and starts r.run in a goroutine; the run body is unread.
Paxos handlers mutate shared instance and ballot state. Their dispatch serialization and interaction with executeCommands require the unread startup and event loop.
executeCommands maintains the application frontier and queues recovery requests.
The client owns proposal sequence numbers and destination selection; server-side request correlation and deduplication are only partially visible.
selection_injection: runReplica selects paxos.New when strings.ToLower(c.Protocol) is paxos.
The master supplies replicaId, nodeList, and isLeader; runReplica separately computes f from len(c.ReplicaAddrs).
paxos.New invokes the built-in replica.New with thrifty=false, exec=true, and lread=false.
replica.New initializes Dreply=true, Durable=false, StableStore=nil, and a fresh state.State. Later assignments have not been inspected.
Logger and configuration objects are passed into the built-in runtime. Their injection does not externalize repository-owned protocol, transport, or storage behavior.
variants: Direct reply after execution when Dreply is true, versus a success reply with an empty value at the accept-reply commit threshold when Dreply is false.
Full Commit carries commands; CommitShort relies on the existing instance representation.
Persistence helpers are disabled when Durable is false and invoke the built-in file interface when it is true; activation and recovery support remain unknown.
Master initial leader selection uses an explicitly configured leader address when present, otherwise measured registration latency.
Client SendProposal selects the leader or closest replica, or broadcasts when Fast is true. Activation of these client flags for the selected deployment is unread.
unknowns: The exact protocol event-loop ownership, goroutine startup, proposal batching, ballot construction, and message destination selection are unread.
The master monitoring and subsequent leadership-transfer paths are unread.
Transport ordering, duplication, peer identity association, disconnect handling, and dispatch failure behavior are unread.
No supplied contract establishes crash-restart support, permitted storage failures, or recovery from persisted files.
No supplied evidence establishes dynamic membership support or its absence.
The package-build capability reports compilation only; no protocol execution or schedule-control evidence is supplied.

activities.purpose: Select and expose master-local leader metadata and request replica leadership.
activities.realization_summary: Registration can mark an initial candidate. Bootstrap and replacement selection call Replica.BeTheLeader and interpret its reply. Monitoring clears marked leaders on ping errors. GetLeader returns the first marked index.

activities.purpose: Resume stalled instance processing through protocol recovery.
activities.realization_summary: The execution loop queues an interval of instance identifiers after a stalled frontier exceeds its grace period. recover initializes missing local structures and invokes makeBallot and bcastPrepare. This establishes a recovery attempt, not recovered participation or restart restoration.

activities.purpose: Maintain the master registration directory and expose participant readiness and availability metadata.
activities.realization_summary: The constructor fixes N and allocates participant arrays. Register assigns indices by address-port identity; GetReplicaList publishes the directory and availability flags after initial monitoring. This is directory management; protocol configuration activation is not established.

unknowns: How replicas consume this directory as protocol membership remains unread.
No removal or resizing mechanism appears in this file; repository-wide participant-change applicability remains unresolved.

activities.purpose: Consume locally committed instances in frontier order and invoke state-machine operations.
activities.realization_summary: executeCommands visits the next instance through crtInstance, stops at the first missing, commandless, or noncommitted record, and advances executedUpTo after processing an eligible batch. Direct-reply ownership controls whether all commands execute or only PUT commands execute.

Other cases execute only PUT commands before advancing the frontier
unknowns: Concrete command execution semantics
Synchronization with instance replacement and mutation

activities.purpose: Maintain instance history and optional persistence used by protocol and execution consumers.
activities.realization_summary: Instance history resides in a preallocated pointer array. Optional helpers serialize bal and status, serialize commands, and call Sync. Visible call sites differ in which helpers they invoke. Helpers do not inspect file Write or Sync results, and no durable-completion fact is established here.

activities.purpose: Preserve client operation identity through submission, local protocol processing, and reply emission.
activities.realization_summary: Clients assign sequence numbers and send proposals with client identity. Leader bookkeeping retains proposal objects. Full commit processing can requeue them. Success replies arise either at local commit marking or after execution depending on Dreply.

facts.validity_context: After the registration handler has populated the directory entry. This does not establish successful replica startup, protocol membership activation, or current availability.
facts.durability: In-memory only in the supplied source.
facts.recovery: No restoration path is shown; a fresh constructor creates an empty directory.
unknowns: Caller registration retries and restart identity semantics are unread.

facts.meaning: The master currently marks a replica index as a selected leader in its local metadata.
facts.validity_context: While the corresponding leader flag remains true. Registration can establish this mark before any leadership RPC. The mark alone establishes neither unique leadership nor completed replica authority.
facts.recovery: Fresh startup initializes flags to false and can mark candidates through registration and leadership replies.
unknowns: Consumers outside GetLeader and the master loop are unread.
Concurrent visibility is unresolved because not all writers hold master.lock.

facts.meaning: For a replica index, the master has stored whether the most recently processed Ping call returned without error.
facts.validity_context: After a ping result has been assigned to alive[index], until another result replaces it. It describes a completed call outcome, not continued reachability or legal protocol participation.
facts.durability: In-memory only; no timestamp or generation accompanies the boolean.
facts.recovery: Bootstrap recomputes values through an initial ping pass.
unknowns: The false constructor value does not distinguish an unobserved replica from a failed ping.
Remote Ping behavior and periodic-read synchronization are unresolved.

facts.meaning: The bootstrap goroutine completed its initial pass of ping calls over nodes and published initialization completion.
facts.validity_context: After finishInit is set under master.lock. Completion includes ping errors and does not assert that all replicas are alive or that leadership replacement has completed.
facts.durability: In-memory monotonic flag within the shown process lifetime.
facts.recovery: A fresh master starts with finishInit=false and repeats bootstrap.
unknowns: No bounded initialization duration is established; dialing and RPC calls can delay publication.
